name: Forest-Section Coefficient-Ratio Maximum Law
statement: Under common-section gluing with pairwise disjoint downward-closed private blocks, if the section incidence graph $G_D$ is a forest, then $\tau(X)=\max_j\tau(C_j)$, including when some pieces are nonrealizable.
proof: On a forest, any two positive section coefficient arrays differ by positive row and coordinate rescalings: solve their logarithmic edge differences successively from a root in every tree. Coordinate rescaling can be canceled in witness magnitudes and row rescaling does not change ratios. Hence near-optimal piece arrays can be made identical on the section and glued, proving the upper bound; restriction to each piece proves the lower bound. Equivalently, the entropy interface cycle space is zero.
comments: This exact coefficient-ratio identity is stronger than the positive-margin bounds recorded in the forest-section gluing theorem.
